questions.stem: According to collision theory, two conditions must be met for a reaction to occur. Which pair of conditions is correct?

options.text: Particles must collide and the temperature must be high
Particles must collide with sufficient energy and with the correct orientation
Particles must be in solution and a catalyst must be present
Particles must collide and a catalyst must lower the activation energy

questions.explanation: For a reaction to occur, particles must collide with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy (sufficient energy) AND they must collide in the correct orientation so that the reactive parts of the molecules come into contact. Not every collision leads to a reaction - only those meeting both conditions are 'successful collisions'.

questions.stem: A student doubles the concentration of hydrochloric acid in a reaction with magnesium. Using collision theory, explain why the rate approximately doubles.

options.text: The acid particles move twice as fast
There are twice as many acid particles in the same volume, so the frequency of collisions approximately doubles
The activation energy is halved
The particles now have twice as much energy

questions.explanation: Doubling the concentration means there are twice as many HCl particles in the same volume. This means they collide with the magnesium surface approximately twice as often (doubled collision frequency). The energy of individual particles and the activation energy are unchanged - it is purely an increase in how often collisions occur.

questions.stem: Increasing temperature increases reaction rate in two ways according to collision theory. Which two effects does higher temperature have?

options.text: Particles collide more often AND a greater proportion of collisions exceed the activation energy
Particles get larger AND collide more often
The activation energy is lowered AND particles collide more often
Particles collide more often AND the concentration increases

questions.explanation: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy. This has two effects: (1) particles move faster, so they collide more frequently, and (2) a greater proportion of these collisions have energy exceeding the activation energy, so more collisions are successful. The second effect is the more significant of the two.

questions.stem: A lump of zinc reacts slowly with dilute acid, but zinc powder reacts vigorously. Both have the same mass. Using collision theory, why does the powder react faster?

options.text: The powder has a higher temperature than the lump
The powder has a greater surface area, exposing more zinc particles to acid collisions
The powder has more zinc atoms than the lump
The powder lowers the activation energy of the reaction

questions.explanation: The powder has a much greater total surface area than the lump (same mass but many tiny particles instead of one large piece). More zinc atoms are exposed at the surface, so more collisions between acid particles and zinc can occur per second. The frequency of successful collisions increases, so the rate increases. The mass, temperature, and activation energy are all the same.

questions.stem: In an industrial reactor, increasing the pressure of gaseous reactants increases the reaction rate. Which explanation using collision theory is correct?

options.text: Higher pressure gives particles more energy to overcome the activation energy
Higher pressure forces particles into the correct orientation
Higher pressure pushes gas particles closer together, increasing the frequency of collisions
Higher pressure acts as a catalyst by lowering the activation energy

questions.explanation: Increasing pressure reduces the volume, forcing gas particles closer together. This is equivalent to increasing concentration - there are more particles per unit volume. The particles collide more frequently, increasing the number of successful collisions per second. Pressure does not change particle energy or activation energy.
